plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-12 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Financial Technology program page (poid=11089) and its linked official degree map, 'Financial Technology Degree Maps (2026-2027)', tab 'Financial Technology (Campus)', last updated/reviewed July 27, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. All courses must be passed with a C- (1.7) or better to be counted in the major (catalog program information); credits older than 10 years must be approved by the CSCY Department Chair before being allowed to count towards the major (catalog program information). Every semester's courses sum to the map's printed semester total (16/13/15/15/15/15/16/15) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BS Degree: 120. The catalog curriculum is exercised exactly by the map: Mathematics Requirements 16 at the exercised values (CS 2300 3 + MATH 1050 4 + Statistics/Data Science choice 3 (map: MATH 1190) + Calculus choice 3 (map: MATH 1100) + Applied Mathematics choice 3 (map: MATH 3150); the catalog prints the block as a 16-18 credit range); Computer Science & Cybersecurity Requirements 27 (nine 3-credit courses, all placed on the map); Business Requirements 27 (eight 3-credit courses plus the Economics choice 3); Additional Support Requirements 9 (Communication, Ethics and Project Management choices 3 each; the map prints COMM 1010 for the Communication choice and generic labels for the other two); Financial Technology Electives 12 (the map's one 'Major FinTech Elective' row plus its three 'Major Upper-division Elective' rows). The catalog's block totals (BS Degree Requirement 12 + General Education 28+ + Curriculum 91-93) exceed 120 if added naively because the catalog states that a portion of the BS requirements may be met by fulfilling the General Education areas and several curriculum courses carry GE tags (MATH 1050, the statistics and calculus choices, the Economics choice, COMM 1010, CSCY 2400); the map's placement is the university's own reconciliation to 120. Catalog course titles are recorded where the map shortens them (MATH 1190 Introduction to Data Science; CS 2420 Introduction to Algorithms and Data Structures; CSCY 3200 Database Design and Management; CSCY 1200 Critical Thinking for Logic and Design). The map's free rows total 10 credits (3 + 3 + 4), recorded as printed; the catalog prints no fixed free-elective figure.
